stanzas.sanskrit:
मतिरिह गुणसक्ता बन्धकृत् तेष्वसक्ता
त्वमृतकृदुपरुन्धे भक्तियोगस्तु सक्तिम् ।
महदनुगमलभ्या भक्तिरेवात्र साध्या
कपिलतनुरिति त्वं देवहूत्यै न्यगादीः ॥ १५-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Bhagwan who was incarnate as Kapila instructed Devahuti that in this world when the intellect gets attached to the sense objects, it becomes the cause of bondage. Otherwise, it leads to liberation. The path of devotion indeed prevents attachment and this alone has to be sought.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
matiriha guṇasaktā bandhakṛt teṣvasaktā
tvamṛtakṛduparundhe bhaktiyogastu saktim |
mahadanugamalabhyā bhaktirevātra sādhyā
kapilatanuriti tvaṃ devahūtyai nyagādīḥ || 15-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
प्रकृतिमहदहङ्काराश्च मात्राश्च भूता-
-न्यपि हृदपि दशाक्षी पूरुषः पञ्चविंशः ।
इति विदितविभागो मुच्यतेऽसौ प्रकृत्या
कपिलतनुरिति त्वं देवहूत्यै न्यगादीः ॥ १५-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
Bhagwan who was incarnate as Kapila further instructed Devahuti that
Prakriti, (Primordial Nature),
Mahat-tatva (the great Spirit),
Ahankaara (I sense),
the five Tanmaatraas (sound, smell, touch, form, taste),
the five Bhootaas (subtle elements- space,air,fire, water, earth),
Antahkarana (mind and its various modes),
the ten Indriyaas (Organs, five of knowledge-hearing, seeing, touch, taste smell, and five of action-speech,hands,legs,anus,genitals),
and
Purush (Atman), these are the twentyfive categories.
When the Purusha realizes the distinctiveness of these categories, he is liberated from the bondage of Prakriti.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
prakṛtimahadahaṅkārāśca mātrāśca bhūtā-
-nyapi hṛdapi daśākṣī pūruṣaḥ pañcaviṃśaḥ |
iti viditavibhāgo mucyate’sau prakṛtyā
kapilatanuriti tvaṃ devahūtyai nyagādīḥ || 15-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
प्रकृतिगतगुणौघैर्नाज्यते पूरुषोऽयं
यदि तु सजति तस्यां तद्गुणास्तं भजेरन् ।
मदनुभजनतत्त्वालोचनैः साप्यपेयात्
कपिलतनुरिति त्वं देवहूत्यै न्यगादीः ॥ १५-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Kapila further instructed Devahuti that the Purusha, by itself, is free from the attributes of Prakriti, but if he identifies himself with Prakriti, then the attributes of Prakriti attach themselves to him. Prakriti will leave its hold on Purusha if he constantly worships Bhagwan.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
prakṛtigataguṇaughairnājyate pūruṣo’yaṃ
yadi tu sajati tasyāṃ tadguṇāstaṃ bhajeran |
madanubhajanatattvālocanaiḥ sāpyapeyāt
kapilatanuriti tvaṃ devahūtyai nyagādīḥ || 15-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
विमलमतिरुपात्तैरासनाद्यैर्मदङ्गं
गरुडसमधिरूढं दिव्यभूषायुधाङ्कम् ।
रुचितुलिततमालं शीलयेतानुवेलं
कपिलतनुरिति त्वं देवहूत्यै न्यगादीः ॥ १५-४ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Having purified the mind by control of the senses and by meditative postures, one should constantly meditate on Bhagwan, adorned with divine ornaments and weapons, seated on Garuda  were the further instructions to Devahuti  by Kapila.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
vimalamatirupāttairāsanādyairmadaṅgaṃ
garuḍasamadhirūḍhaṃ divyabhūṣāyudhāṅkam |
rucitulitatamālaṃ śīlayetānuvelaṃ
kapilatanuriti tvaṃ devahūtyai nyagādīḥ || 15-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
मम गुणगणलीलाकर्णनैः कीर्तनाद्यैः
मयि सुरसरिदोघप्रख्यचित्तानुवृत्तिः ।
भवति परमभक्तिः सा हि मृत्योर्विजेत्री
कपिलतनुरिति त्वं देवहूत्यै न्यगादीः ॥ १५-५ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Kapila instructed Devahuti that by regularly listening to Bhagwan’s excellences,  sportive deeds and by chanting Bhagwan’s name, the supreme devotion is born. This devotion in which the mind flows in an uninterrupted stream towards Bhagwan, like the Ganga flows towards the sea, alone can conquer the cycle of birth and death.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
mama guṇagaṇalīlākarṇanaiḥ kīrtanādyaiḥ
mayi surasaridoghaprakhyacittānuvṛttiḥ |
bhavati paramabhaktiḥ sā hi mṛtyorvijetrī
kapilatanuriti tvaṃ devahūtyai nyagādīḥ || 15-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अहह बहुलहिंसासञ्चितार्थैः कुटुम्बं
प्रतिदिनमनुपुष्णन् स्त्रीजितो बाललाली ।
विशति हि गृहसक्तो यातनां मय्यभक्तः
कपिलतनुरिति त्वं देवहूत्यै न्यगादीः ॥ १५-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Kapila instructed Devahuti that earning and acquiring wealth by unfair means, attachment to children and other worldly possessions without devotion to Bhagwan leads to sufferings at hell.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
ahaha bahulahiṃsāsañcitārthaiḥ kuṭumbaṃ
pratidinamanupuṣṇan strījito bālalālī |
viśati hi gṛhasakto yātanāṃ mayyabhaktaḥ
kapilatanuriti tvaṃ devahūtyai nyagādīḥ || 15-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
युवतिजठरखिन्नो जातबोधोऽप्यकाण्डे
प्रसवगलितबोधः पीडयोल्लङ्घ्य बाल्यम् ।
पुनरपि बत मुह्यत्येव तारुण्यकाले
कपिलतनुरिति त्वं देवहूत्यै न्यगादीः ॥ १५-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Kapila instructed Devahuti that the Jeeva on entering the mother's womb remembers the association with Bhagwan until it is born. The minute it falls in to the world, the child forgets the association, suffers through childhood, attains youth and again get infatuated by the materialistic life.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
yuvatijaṭharakhinno jātabodho’pyakāṇḍe
prasavagalitabodhaḥ pīḍayollaṅghya bālyam |
punarapi bata muhyatyeva tāruṇyakāle
kapilatanuriti tvaṃ devahūtyai nyagādīḥ || 15-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
पितृसुरगणयाजी धार्मिको यो गृहस्थः
स च निपतति काले दक्षिणाध्वोपगामी ।
मयि निहितमकामं कर्म तूदक्पथार्थं
कपिलतनुरिति त्वं देवहूत्यै न्यगादीः ॥ १५-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Kapila instructed Devahuti that a righteous person performing poojas to Devathas and Pithrus go to heaven and and attain birth again after enjoying the fruits of his meritorious deeds. Those who perform the same, dedicating the fruits of deeds to Bhagwan HIMSELF and expect no result and always stay devoted to Bhagwan will eventually attain salvation.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
pitṛsuragaṇayājī dhārmiko yo gṛhasthaḥ
sa ca nipatati kāle dakṣiṇādhvopagāmī |
mayi nihitamakāmaṃ karma tūdakpathārthaṃ
kapilatanuriti tvaṃ devahūtyai nyagādīḥ || 15-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
इति सुविदितवेद्यां देव हे देवहूतिं
कृतनुतिमनुगृह्य त्वं गतो योगिसङ्घैः ।
विमलमतिरथाऽसौ भक्तियोगेन मुक्ता
त्वमपि जनहितार्थं वर्तसे प्रागुदीच्याम् ॥ १५-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Following the advice of Kapila, Mother Devahuti was liberated from worldly attachments and attained salvation by following the path of devotion. Lord Kapila left with group of sanyasis in the North east direction and stays there even now for the good of the people.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
iti suviditavedyāṃ deva he devahūtiṃ
kṛtanutimanugṛhya tvaṃ gato yogisaṅghaiḥ |
vimalamatirathā’sau bhaktiyogena muktā
tvamapi janahitārthaṃ vartase prāgudīcyām || 15-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
परम किमु बहूक्त्या त्वत्पदाम्भोजभक्तिं
सकलभयविनेत्रीं सर्वकामोपनेत्रीम् ।
वदसि खलु दृढं त्वं तद्विधूयामयान्मे
गुरुपवनपुरेश त्वय्युपाधत्स्व भक्तिम् ॥ १५-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Declaring once again that firm devotion to Bhagwan will remove all fears and sufferings, Bhattathiri  requested Guruvayoorappan  to cure his afflictions and to endow him with devotion to Bhagwan.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
parama kimu bahūktyā tvatpadāmbhojabhaktiṃ
sakalabhayavinetrīṃ sarvakāmopanetrīm |
vadasi khalu dṛḍhaṃ tvaṃ tadvidhūyāmayānme
gurupavanapureśa tvayyupādhatsva bhaktim || 15-10 ||
